purpose: Every implementation this corpus has been replayed against, with the one field that decides whether a number may be quoted: independence. A row is a fact about a run, not a claim about a product.
independence_rule: independent = different maintainer, writes its verifier from the spec text without reading this repository's reference code. same-maintainer = one of us. Everything else is a guess and is refused by tools/check_implementations.py.

maintainer.note: A single-operator corpus. That is why this file exists at all: the honest label is cheaper than an overclaim someone else disproves later.

implementations.coverage_note: Runs all 19 checks; invented the corpus it is measured against.
No shared code with the reference. Anchors, merkle proofs, RFC 3161 tokens and policy artefacts (S9, S10, S13-S19) are outside its declared scope and are not scored.

evidence.note: These four numbers are not prose. tools/check_implementations.py recomputes them from interop-results.json and refuses the file when they drift, so a stale number here fails CI instead of impressing a reader.

known_divergences.what: The specification text did not say whether the evidence root is computed over bytes on disk or over hashes claimed in evidence/index.json. The reference computes it over bytes on disk, reports S5 as skipped (INCONCLUSIVE) when S4 fails, and marks S8 FAIL when the checkpoint over on-disk bytes differs.
known_divergences.consequence: The second implementation first reported S5/S8 as PASS on tampered and deleted packages - arithmetically true, semantically worthless. Caught by the per-check comparison on 2026-11-24, fixed in the same run, and the rule is now stated in the implementation comment where a reader will meet it.

how_to_add_a_third_implementation.1: Open a pull request adding one object here with independence set to 'independent' and the checks you actually run.
how_to_add_a_third_implementation.2: Attach the machine output of tools/run_crossimpl.py against your implementation, or your own results file in the same shape as interop-results.json.
how_to_add_a_third_implementation.3: A row claiming 'independent' from the same maintainer address is refused by tools/check_implementations.py - the label is checked, not trusted.
how_to_add_a_third_implementation.4: The gate does not certify your product. It records that a run happened and that its verdicts matched.
